our_title: kgraphMapRb() merges fixed vertices and computes frontier and cost after the recursive bipartitioning failed
ran:
$WORK/repro/GRA-21/gra21.32 100 h (pristine, hcub target, invalid fixed terminal): ERROR: kgraphMapRbBgraph: invalid fixed part array / kgraphMapRbMap: cannot create bipartition graph ; then arch_hcub.c:261:13: runtime error: shift exponent -1094795586 is negative (#0 archHcubDomSize #1 kgraphCost kgraph_cost.c:179 #2 kgraphMapRb kgraph_map_rb.c:176) ; kgraph_cost.c:178:34: runtime error: signed integer overflow ; ret=1.
Patched: the two errors, 'kgraphMapRb: cannot compute recursive bipartitioning', ret=1, no sanitizer report.

fix_options.label: Return as soon as the recursion fails (recommended)
fix_options.summary: Free vflotab / indgrafdat, then return 1 before merging, frontier and cost computations.
fix_options.tradeoffs: One more error message in the chain.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Same early-return-on-error structure as the rest of the routine.

fix_options.label: Skip only the cost computations
fix_options.summary: Guard Merge and the cost block with o == 0, keep return (o).
fix_options.tested: untested: equivalent by reading, two guards instead of one exit.

our_title: Mapping strategies that do not start with a method computing an initial mapping dereference a NULL part array
ran:
From <tree>/src/check, pristine and patched alike: gpart 4 data/m16x16.grf /dev/null -vmt -Mf -> kgraph_cost.c:104:13: runtime error: load of null pointer of type 'Anum' (#0 kgraphCost #1 kgraphMapFm #2 kgraphMapSt) ; '-Mb{width=3,bnd=f,org=f}' -> same via kgraphMapBd ; '-Md{pass=10}' -> AddressSanitizer: SEGV ; -Mx -> 'Processors 0/4 (0)'.
With alt/PS2-G12-2-a applied to a scratch tree (library_graph_map.c: mapAlloc + kgraphFrst after kgraphInit): all four print 'Processors 1/4 (0.25)', default strategy unchanged (4/4).
location_7_0_17: src/libscotch/library_graph_map.c:272-294 (kgraphInit then kgraphMapSt without mapAlloc); src/libscotch/kgraph.c:116-117 (mapInit leaves m.parttax NULL); consumers src/libscotch/kgraph_cost.c:104, kgraph_map_fm.c, kgraph_map_df.c, kgraph_map_bd.c:155
evidence:
kgraph.c:116: mapInit (&actgrafptr->m, &actgrafptr->s, archptr, domnptr); /* Compute m.domnmax */ -- no part array
kgraph_map_ml.c:245-249: if (mapAlloc (&finegrafptr->m) != 0) ... kgraphFrst (finegrafptr); /* Assign all vertices to first subdomain */ -- only the multilevel and RB methods allocate
kgraph_cost.c:104: partval = parttax[vertnum]; (parttax == NULL)

fix_options.label: Allocate and initialise the mapping in graphMapCompute2() (sketch, other group's file)
fix_options.summary: mapAlloc (&mapgrafdat.m) + kgraphFrst (&mapgrafdat) right after kgraphInit(), so every method starts from 'all vertices in the initial domain'.
fix_options.tested: built in a scratch tree and run as above (no crash, 1/4 parts); not run through the check suite; PT-Scotch twin (library_dgraph_map.c) not examined.
fix_options.tradeoffs: One extra allocation per API call (freed by kgraphExit); strategies without an initial method now return the trivial mapping instead of crashing.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Same two calls as kgraph_map_ml.c:245-249; could alternatively live in kgraphInit() (kgraph.c), which the maintainer may prefer.

fix_options.label: Reject strategies whose first method needs a mapping
fix_options.summary: In kgraphMapSt(), errorPrint and return 1 when m.parttax == NULL for refinement methods.
fix_options.tested: untested: not written, needs a per-method flag in the strategy table.
fix_options.tradeoffs: User-visible error instead of a trivial result.

our_title: Deterministic option ignored by the context split of recursive bipartitioning: results depend on the number of threads
ran:
repro/PS2-G12-3/run.sh <lib> <bin> <check dir>: SCOTCH_DETERMINISTIC=1, SCOTCH_PTHREAD_NUMBER=1/2/4, gpart -o 9 bump.grf -Mr{sep=f} (sequential vgraph separators only) and gpart 9 bump.grf -Cr; diff line counts between the map files (each single run is reproducible: same run twice -> 0):
  G08's tree (7.0.17 + bgraphBipartGg determinism fixes, this item unfixed): ovl t1-vs-t2=16606 t2-vs-t4=7132 ; rb 4732 / 428
  G08's tree + this patch (kgraph_map_rb_part.c, wgraph_part_rb.c): ovl 0 / 0 ; rb 0 / 0
  this series alone ($WORK/build, no GG fix): ovl 0 / 0 ; rb t1-vs-t2=0 t2-vs-t4=4304 (remaining difference is bgraphBipartGg's pass sharing, PS2-G08-1/SEP-13).
location_7_0_17: src/libscotch/kgraph_map_rb_part.c:315-322; src/libscotch/wgraph_part_rb.c:376-383; src/libscotch/common_context.c:283-299 (contextThreadLaunchSplit creates a second pseudo-random generator)

fix_options.label: Do not split the context when deterministic behaviour is wanted (recommended)
fix_options.summary: In kgraphMapRbPart2() and wgraphPartRb2(), read CONTEXTOPTIONNUMDETERMINISTIC and run the two sub-tasks in sequence within the same context when it is set, exactly like graphMatchInit() falls back to sequential matching.
fix_options.tested: determinism runs above (1 == 2 == 4 threads once combined with G08's GG fix; overlap path already 1 == 2 == 4 with this series alone); zero warnings on 32/64-bit; check_prog_gpart, check_prog_gpart_overlap, check_scotch_graph_map on 32/64/debug builds.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Deterministic mode loses the recursion-level parallelism (each sub-task still uses all threads of the context for its own threaded methods, which are sequential in deterministic mode anyway). Non-deterministic mode unchanged.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Caller-side check with the exact idiom of graph_match.c:205-225 (common_context.c cannot include context.h: the option enum is libscotch-level). 'Document that deterministic needs >= 2 threads' is not an option: the documentation already promises 'for any number of threads' and 2 and 4 threads differ as well (the split recurses).

fix_options.label: Always derive the second sub-task's generator, even when running sequentially
fix_options.summary: Make contextThreadLaunchSplit() draw the second generator and run the two sub-tasks itself when the context has a single thread, so that the pseudo-random streams are identical for every thread count without losing parallelism.
fix_options.tested: untested: changes the results of every single-threaded run (COMMON_RANDOM_FIXED_SEED results change between versions), touches the common layer used by all callers, and still requires every threaded method to be thread-count independent.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Keeps parallelism in deterministic mode; larger behaviour change.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: A design change he may prefer for 7.1, not a 7.0.x bugfix.

our_title: Hash table sizes computed with an int shift `1 << (hashsiz + 2)` overflow for more than 2^29 entries
why_not_run: needs more than 2^29 fixed vertices (or domains) to overflow; not constructible on this machine
evidence: kgraph_map_rb.c:243: hashsiz = 1 << (hashsiz + 2); /* Fill hash table at 25% maximum */ (hashsiz is Gnum, the shifted constant is int)

fix_options.label: Shift a Gnum constant
fix_options.tested: untested: not written as a diff (trivial, and the maintainer's 7.0.17 bit-set fix 6a00c51 used unsigned constants, so he may prefer (Gunum) 1).
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Same class as his 'apply left shifts to unsigned integers' fix.
